title: A projective bundle is separated over its base
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal E$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module, and let $\pi:\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)=\operatorname{Proj}_S(\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_S}\mathcal E)\to S$ be the associated projective-bundle morphism [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. Then $\pi$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism].

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_S}(\mathcal E)$. By [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], the given $\pi$ is $\operatorname{Proj}_S(\mathcal A)\to S$. The symmetric-algebra sheaf is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra]. Its grading by symmetric degree is the grading of [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded], realized on affine sections by [def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra]. Thus it is an input of the relative-Proj construction. No finite-type or local-freeness hypothesis on $\mathcal E$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 01OB, constructions-definition-projective-bundle and the paragraph preceding it (symmetric algebra quasi-coherent and graded)

proof.text: For each affine open $U\subseteq S$, set $C_U=\Gamma(U,\mathcal A)$ and $P_U=\pi^{-1}(U)$. The relative-Proj affine restriction theorem [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists] identifies $P_U$ with $\operatorname{Proj}(C_U)$, compatibly with its structural morphism $p_U:P_U\to U$. In [def-nagata-relative-proj] this structural map is explicitly the Proj degree-zero map followed by the spectrum map induced by $\mathcal O_S(U)\to (C_U)_0$. In particular the local model is an ordinary Proj of a graded ring; it is not asserted to be affine or to be projective space.

source.place: Tag 01O2, constructions-lemma-relative-proj-separated, affine restriction sentence; construction in Tag 01NY, constructions-lemma-relative-proj

proof.text: By [lem-trf-proj-separated] the scheme $\operatorname{Proj}(C_U)$ is separated, so its canonical morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is separated. The composite of $p_U:P_U\to U$ with the canonical $U\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is that same morphism under the isomorphism of Step 2. Apply clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation] to this composite to obtain that $p_U$ is separated. No separatedness of $S$ and no finite-generation condition on $C_U$ is used.

source.place: Tag 01O2, constructions-lemma-relative-proj-separated, using Tag 01MC (Proj separated) and Schemes Tag 01KV (separated cancellation)

proof.text: Write $P=\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)$, $Q=P\times_SP$, and $q:Q\to S$ for the common base map. The open subschemes $W_U=q^{-1}(U)$ for affine opens $U\subseteq S$ cover $Q$. By the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product], $W_U=P_U\times_U P_U$: maps to either side are exactly pairs of maps to $P$ with equal base map factoring through $U$. Factoring through an open subscheme means restricting the continuous and sheaf maps [def-weil-open-immersion], so this identification is also an identification of the indicated open subschemes. The inverse image of $W_U$ under $\Delta_\pi$ is $P_U$, and the restricted map is $\Delta_{p_U}$ because both its projections are the identity. Step 3 and [def-weil-proper-morphism] say that every such restricted diagonal is a closed immersion. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-finite-etale-zariski-local], applied to the open cover $(W_U)$ of the TARGET $Q$ of the diagonal, makes $\Delta_\pi$ a closed immersion. By [def-weil-proper-morphism] this is precisely separatedness of $\pi$.
